clue.text: Present president, bovine

clue.text: Powerfully rhythmic music in dance

explanation.surface: A description of the beat-heavy music found in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip hop is a genre built on strong beats with rapping, born in 1970s New York.

clue.text: Swimmer hit a bad patch

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to struggle or falter

clue.text: Partial attempt to acquire answer, only odd letters checked

clue.text: Miss held up by partner, abandoned

clue.text: Around Beds town, image of igneous rock

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.walkthrough: Beds is the standard abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county; Luton is its largest town.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutonic rocks such as granite form from magma cooling deep underground, a kind of igneous rock.

clue.text: Solver filling spaces with misspellings, originally

explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is the fictional detective who solves cases, the archetypal solver of crimes.

clue.text: Mammal possibly needing a lift up to catch wings of cuckoo

clue.text: Working with series that's in production

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a line is a series, as of kings or products

explanation.surface: Someone at work alongside a TV series currently being made.

clue.text: For example, one deep colour

second meaning: a deep scarlet red

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both counting numbers in mathematics and a rich scarlet shade, from church robes.

clue.text: Cut, a bit of a fiddle

parts.note: the bridge is part of a violin, holding up the strings

clue.text: Retrieve number from Fab Four

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a song by the Beatles, nicknamed the Fab Four

explanation.walkthrough: Number here is a song, and the Fab Four are the Beatles; Get Back was a 1969 single.

clue.text: PM in hole, did you say?

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground

explanation.walkthrough: PM stands for Prime Minister; both William Pitts held the office in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: William Pitt the Elder and his son the Younger were both British prime ministers.

clue.text: Picture game in pieces

parts.note: snap is a card game
something shot to pieces is shot, broken

explanation.surface: An image of a game, perhaps a jigsaw, still in pieces.

clue.text: Gas ring on with heat evenly spread

clue.text: Number one fish for bird

parts.note: the star is the leading performer, the number one
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A top-quality fish served up as food for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common songbird with glossy speckled plumage, known for huge flocks.

clue.text: Green leaf I angled back, somewhat

somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

explanation.definitionFit: Green can mean inexperienced or innocent, and a naive person is likewise unworldly and artless.

clue.text: Dish is found in cave, unopened

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave

clue.text: Suffering in boy unfortunately very much like it?

parts.note: taken as written
someone ill is suffering

explanation.definitionFit: Like billy-o is an old British idiom meaning very vigorously, so the word completes it.

clue.text: Fill pack currently occupied with minimum of food

names what goes inside the packed word

clue.text: Two or three points, most original

explanation.definitionFit: Newest means the most recent and so the most novel, as original can mean fresh and new.

clue.text: Hot food, cooler serving?

clue.text: House brightly painted?

clue.text: Batting disaster cut in broadcast?

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.definitionFit: A batsman out for nought twice in one match bags a pair, among the worst batting failures.

clue.text: Squeeze, see, in a big way

clue.text: Work on hands I covered primarily in muck
